guidance.procedure: For each hypothesis independently align actor, modality, action, object, quantifier, trigger, conditions and exceptions before selecting evidence. Silence and neighboring topics are unresolved; never infer permission from absence, a trigger from survival, or one relationship from another. Select every original member independently expressing the governing rule, responsive repetition, necessary scope or operative exception. Headings, recitals and consequences are not members merely by proximity, but retain them when they actually supply a governing object, purpose, condition or responsive proposition.

Separate the disposition trigger from its remedy. Return or destruction supports termination disposition only when tied to termination, expiration, completed dealings, abandonment, failure to enter the contemplated relationship, conclusion of the recipient’s need, or an equivalent endpoint. A request-only duty is unresolved, not opposition; destruction is unnecessary because either return or destruction of some covered information suffices. Retention requires an affirmative archive, backup, legal-file, compliance, recordkeeping or document-policy carve-out. Opposition requires an express no-retention or no-copy command, or comprehensive disposition covering all originals, copies and derivatives together with deletion from storage; a bare return duty does not itself settle post-disposition retention. Cite the endpoint and remedy for disposition. For retention, cite the carve-out introduction and every independently retained category, or all operative components establishing exhaustive deletion; never treat a no-retention clause as permission.

Find an identified duty that remains operative beyond termination, expiration, completed dealings or another endpoint. Support survival from express continuation, a post-endpoint duration, indefinite confidentiality obligations, an indefinite agreement governing those obligations, retained material remaining subject to duties, a statement that return does not discharge duties, or other provisions continuing after a particular restriction ends. A finite agreement term without post-endpoint effect, a possible later end date, remedies for an earlier breach or an exception lacking a continuing duty is insufficient. Cite every independently responsive continuation, including return-related continuation, duration language, bilateral repetitions and short connectors necessary to identify what continues; do not substitute an ordinary term clause.

Resolve each definition boundary from the operative qualification routes. Technical-only coverage requires an exhaustive definition confined to technical or comparable system material. An expressly covered business, financial, commercial, personnel or other nontechnical category in that definition opposes it; generic words such as information or data, disclosure media, marking rules and isolated ancillary references do not. Oral coverage requires an operative oral, verbal, spoken, visual, intangible, any-medium or not-reduced-to-writing route. Universal identification requires every route to depend on a discloser’s designation, marking, notice or equivalent identifying act. Objective confidentiality, general confidential character, content, circumstances, reason-to-know, automatic coverage or absence-of-marking language opposes universal identification; mere disclosure by the discloser is not identification. Cite only the governing introduction and alternative routes needed to establish the boundary, including an express no-marking route, rather than adjacent examples or unrelated exclusions.

Decide the two source routes independently. Independent development requires an express exclusion or allowance for development, creation, discovery or acquisition by the receiving party or its personnel without using or accessing protected information; third-party receipt, public availability and generic competitive activity do not substitute. Third-party acquisition requires an express lawful, authorized, unrestricted or nonconfidential third-party source route, preserving knowledge, authorization and no-duty conditions; public availability and recipient development do not substitute. Silence is unresolved, never contradiction or permission. A confidentiality or purpose-use restriction opposes independent development only if it expressly reaches independently created information. Cite the governing exclusion introduction only when it supplies operative scope, then the qualifying branch and every separately operative bilateral repetition or affirmative similar-information permission; omit unrelated branches.

Require an operative standing permission or exception allowing disclosure or access to the relevant recipient class, subject to any need-to-know, purpose, undertaking or confidentiality conditions. Definitions, responsibility clauses and commands that persons protect information do not themselves authorize their access. Evaluate employees separately from nonemployee third parties: employee access alone cannot support third-party sharing, and an undefined representative label supports third-party sharing only when another provision defines it to include consultants, contractors, agents, advisers or another nonemployee class. A blanket ban reaching any person or the relevant class, or disclosure available only through fresh prior consent, opposes that class; a ban limited to third parties does not by itself oppose employee sharing. Cite the permission or operative ban plus only the class definition and conditions needed to resolve scope.

Support no-license from an express no-rights or no-license rule, retained or exclusive ownership, or a property reservation covering confidential information or its intellectual-property rights. Cite every independently operative ownership and reservation provision, including bilateral counterparts, when each governs the protected information. Permission to receive, evaluate, use or disclose information is not a proprietary grant and does not oppose no-license. A license concerning separate marks, products or services is nonresponsive. Oppose no-license only when an affirmative license actually reaches the confidential information or its associated rights; silence remains unresolved.

Inspect confidentiality, announcements, publicity, media and communications provisions for an operative restriction on revealing the agreement or relationship, the nature of the arrangement or services, exchanged information, discussions, negotiations, transaction status, terms, conditions or related facts. A ban qualified by prior consent still supports the prohibitory hypothesis, and language treating these facts as confidential supports when the contract’s nondisclosure duty governs them. An NDA title, generic duty covering only substantive information, named-contact rule, enforcement notice or entire-agreement clause does not settle the issue. Cite the operative prohibition and every separately listed responsive aspect; include a definition or exception only when it supplies the protected agreement-related fact or materially limits the prohibition.

Require a restriction on soliciting, hiring, offering to hire, inducing, recruiting or encouraging departure by the disclosing party’s employees, officers, agents or other representatives. Restrictions limited to customers, suppliers, vendors, business sources, transaction counterparties or designated contacts do not substitute, nor does a general noncompete. Cite the governing restriction and every relevant target subclause or bilateral repetition, while excluding adjacent customer, supplier and business-source restrictions. Preserve duration, contact-level limitations and recruiting or general-advertisement exceptions only when they define the operative employee restriction.

For copying, require an affirmative allowance or an operative exception permitting copies in stated circumstances; an exception inside a prohibition can support limited permission. A command not to copy, reproduce, duplicate, make or retain copies opposes permission, including consent-qualified bans under this annotation convention. Existing copies, return or retention provisions, proprietary notices on copies and backup references do not themselves authorize creating copies. For reverse engineering, require that act or functionally specified decompilation, disassembly or equivalent extraction; ordinary copying, use limits and general development restrictions are insufficient unless they expressly cover the extracting conduct. Cite a shared governing introduction when needed for actor or modality, the responsive act, and any exception defining permission; exclude adjacent retention, ownership or media language.

Require an affirmative notice duty tied to disclosure compelled by law, regulation, subpoena, judicial process or governmental demand. Notice of an unauthorized breach is not responsive. Preserve legal-permission, practicability and advance-timing qualifications. Cite a governing compelled-disclosure introduction when it supplies the trigger or protected object, the notice command, and any separately operative opportunity-to-object language defining the notice’s purpose. Do not cite later minimum-disclosure, authorization, cooperation or confidential-treatment steps unless they independently impose or qualify notice; include bilateral repetitions when each creates the duty.

Support limited use only when an operative rule makes a stated, agreed, evaluation, transaction or performance purpose exclusive, expressly forbids every other purpose, or prohibits unauthorized or unlicensed reuse of the protected information. Language merely directing appropriate, adequate or necessary use in performing work is unresolved unless it clearly excludes other purposes. Match the actor and protected object: nondisclosure, employee access, information-request limits, ownership, assignment, copying, or restrictions concerning separate marks, products or services do not substitute. Scan distinct protected categories and repetitions, citing every independently operative exclusive-purpose restriction plus any governing introduction supplying the object or purpose; omit neighboring disclosure clauses unless they also restrict use.

Decide endpoint disposition and later retention separately. Pattern: “upon request, return or destroy the materials” is unresolved for termination disposition; “when the evaluation, dealings or recipient’s need ends, return or destroy remaining materials” supports it. Either remedy and any covered subset suffice. For retention, “retain one legal copy” or “automated backups need not be erased” supports possession. Conversely, “return all originals and copies without retaining reproductions,” “destroy every copy,” or return plus deletion from storage opposes retention; a bare return of materials does not. Cite the endpoint and remedy for disposition. For retention cite the carve-out introduction and every independently retained category, or every operative component establishing comprehensive copy removal.

operations.rationale: Request-only duties were repeatedly converted into termination duties, while express no-copy disposition and affirmative retention categories were misclassified or incompletely cited.

guidance.procedure: Test whether the operative coverage is exhaustively technical. A definition confined to technical, engineering, software or comparable system material supports technical-only coverage. A concrete covered route for business, financial, commercial, operational, personnel, lease, marketing, customer, private or internal material opposes it. Generic “information” or “data,” disclosure media, marking rules and an isolated reference outside the coverage definition are unresolved. If the definition incorporates subject matter supplied by a recital or another clause, inspect and cite that incorporated content. Pattern: “technical specifications and source code” may support; “technical specifications, pricing and customer plans” opposes; “information furnished for discussions” alone does neither. Cite the governing definition and only the incorporated or listed routes needed to establish the boundary.

operations.rationale: The combined definition record obscured three different tests. Technical-only errors arose from both treating generic information as nontechnical and overlooking incorporated concrete nontechnical subject matter.

guidance.procedure: Ask whether every route into protected information depends on an identifying act by the discloser. Pattern: “confidential information means material marked or designated confidential” supports universal identification when no alternative route exists. “Marked confidential or reasonably understood from its character or circumstances to be confidential” opposes it because the objective route needs no designation. “All information disclosed by the owner” is unresolved: source identity is not identification. Oral information becoming protected after a later written summary does not by itself prove that every item must be identified as confidential. Cite the definition lead and every alternative qualification route needed to resolve universality, including an express absence-of-marking route; omit examples and exclusions that do not change the identification condition.

operations.rationale: The lawyer treated mere disclosure by an owner as identification, missed marking-only coverage, and repeatedly omitted alternative objective-confidentiality routes.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative route that brings nonwritten disclosure into the protected set. Oral, verbal, spoken, heard, visual, not-reduced-to-writing, or a rule protecting an oral disclosure after a required written confirmation supports. A generic statement that information exists “in any form” is unresolved unless its context unmistakably addresses disclosure media. A command not to disclose protected material verbally regulates the recipient’s act and does not show that verbally received material is covered. Pattern: “oral or written disclosures are confidential” supports; “do not reveal information orally or in writing” does not. Cite the definition or confirmation route and any independently operative continuation specifically governing oral material, not adjacent marking or use provisions.

operations.rationale: Generic form language and a verbal nondisclosure method were mistaken for oral-information inclusion, while genuine oral-confirmation routes were generally reliable.

guidance.procedure: Resolve the two source routes independently. Independent development needs an express exclusion or allowance for creation, development, discovery or acquisition by the recipient or its personnel without using or accessing protected information. A separate affirmative statement that similar or competing products may be developed also supports. Prior possession, public availability, third-party receipt, silence and generic competitive activity do not substitute. Third-party acquisition needs an express lawful, authorized, unrestricted or nonconfidential third-party source route, preserving knowledge, authorization and no-duty conditions; recipient development does not substitute. Pattern: “previously possessed or received from an unrestricted source” supports only the stated routes, not independent development. Cite the operative exclusion introduction, qualifying branch, and every separately operative similar-information permission; omit unrelated exclusion branches.

operations.rationale: The lawyer continued substituting prior possession, public information, silence and the other source route, and routinely omitted exclusion introductions or separate future-development permissions.

guidance.procedure: Find a standing permission or exception allowing the relevant class to receive or access the protected material. Pattern: “may disclose to representatives,” with representatives defined to include employees and advisers, supports both employee and nonemployee sharing; cite the permission, needed definition and operative need-to-know or confidentiality conditions. “Limit access to employees who need it” supports employees but does not support third parties. It opposes third-party sharing only when paired with a ban reaching third parties or everyone else. A fresh-consent-only route or blanket no-disclosure command opposes the covered class. A definition, liability clause or command to protect information is not permission, but a clause expressly recognizing that named persons may receive or access can complete an otherwise elliptical permission. Exclude pure countersignature, breach and responsibility provisions.

operations.rationale: Employee and nonemployee classes remained conflated; definitions and responsibility language were overused, while necessary class definitions, recipient branches and access conditions were frequently omitted.

guidance.procedure: Support no-license from an express no-rights or no-license rule, retained or exclusive ownership, or a property reservation covering the protected information or associated intellectual-property rights. Pattern: “the information remains the owner’s property and no license is granted” supports; “no rights are acquired except limited use for the project” also supports because the purpose-use privilege is not a proprietary grant. A warranty disclaimer, no-commitment clause, permission to evaluate, or silence does not establish no-license. A license concerning separate marks, products or services is nonresponsive. Oppose only when an affirmative license actually reaches the protected information or its associated rights. Cite each independently operative ownership, rights-reservation and no-license provision, including bilateral counterparts.

operations.rationale: The lawyer inferred no-license from unrelated disclaimers, yet missed express no-rights language and ownership provisions.

guidance.procedure: Copy permission requires an affirmative allowance or an exception that itself authorizes making copies in stated circumstances. Pattern: “a limited number of copies may be made for the permitted evaluation” supports. A command not to copy, reproduce, duplicate, make or retain copies opposes permission, including consent-gated bans. A negative clause containing an external requirement is not permission merely because it uses “unless”; decide whether the exception actually grants the recipient authority to copy. Existing copies, return or retention provisions, notices placed on copies, backup references and references to documents do not authorize creation. Cite the governing introduction, responsive copying act and any operative permission-defining exception; exclude ownership, storage and use language.

operations.rationale: Copying and reverse engineering use different observable tests. Copy verdicts were still inferred from unrelated document or use language, and qualified prohibitions were handled inconsistently.

guidance.procedure: Look for reverse engineering by name or a functionally specified extraction act. Pattern: “do not analyze a sample to determine its chemical structure or composition” supports a reverse-engineering prohibition even without that label. Decompiling, disassembling, decoding or extracting design or composition likewise supports when applied to the protected object. Authorization to test or evaluate, ordinary copying restrictions, purpose-use limits, development restrictions and generic nondisclosure do not substitute unless they expressly prohibit the extracting conduct. Cite any short governing introduction needed for actor or object together with every responsive extraction prohibition; do not cite adjacent sample-security, copying or evaluation provisions.

operations.rationale: A functional chemical-composition analysis ban was missed because the prior combined rule did not make the reverse-engineering boundary executable enough.

guidance.procedure: Inspect confidentiality, announcements, publicity and communications provisions for a duty covering agreement-related facts: existence of the agreement or relationship, fact of exchanged access, transaction communications, discussions or negotiations, status, terms, conditions or arrangement. Pattern: “communications between the parties concerning the contemplated transaction are confidential” supports when an operative nondisclosure duty governs those communications; “information furnished about the business is confidential” alone does not. A rule forbidding disclosure that the subject of an exchange is known to the parties can support the fact of the confidential exchange, but a ban on associating oneself with a customer or using a name alone is unresolved. Cite the operative duty and each separately responsive listed fact, plus a definition only when it supplies that fact.

operations.rationale: Transaction communications and the fact of an information exchange were overlooked, while neighboring relationship or substantive-information language required a clearer boundary.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative restriction on approaching, soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing or offering something to a protected person. Employee-focused patterns include bans on soliciting or hiring the discloser’s employees, officers, agents or consultants, subject to stated duration and general-advertisement or unsolicited-contact exceptions. A solicitation/contact provision can also be responsive when it forbids approaching or offering outsiders participation in the contemplated transaction, such as an equity or joint-acquisition role; distinguish this from a clause merely regulating whether the transaction may close. Customer, supplier, business-source and named-contact limits otherwise do not establish representative solicitation. Cite the operative restriction and responsive target or participation branch, excluding adjacent standstill and communication provisions.

operations.rationale: The existing rule categorically excluded a transaction-participation offer that the supplied annotation treated as solicitation, causing the only current solicitation error.

guidance.procedure: Identify both the duty and the endpoint it can outlast. Express continuation after termination, expiration, completed dealings or return supports. So does a confidentiality duration that can extend beyond an independently available termination point, an indefinite protected-duty period, retained material remaining subject to duties, or a statement that disposition does not discharge duties. Pattern: “either party may terminate at any time; confidentiality continues for five years” supports; “the agreement lasts five years” alone does not. A request-only return duty, later possible end date, remedy for an earlier breach or exception without a continuing duty is insufficient. Cite every separately responsive continuation or duration provision and short connector needed to identify what continues, but not an ordinary term clause merely because it states a date.

operations.rationale: The lawyer inferred survival from request-based disposition and ordinary terms, missed fixed or indefinite continuing duties, and often cited a term clause instead of the operative continuation.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative rule making a stated evaluation, transaction, project, business-relationship or performance purpose exclusive. Pattern: “use only to evaluate the transaction” supports; “use as appropriate in performing work” is unresolved because it does not exclude other purposes. A total use ban without any stated permitted purpose is also unresolved for this hypothesis, not opposition. A ban on use for personal benefit can support when an “except as permitted here” route supplies the contract’s stated purpose. Match actor and protected object: nondisclosure, employee access, information-request limits, ownership, assignment and copying do not substitute. Cite every independently operative exclusive-purpose restriction and any governing introduction supplying its object or purpose; omit disclosure-only neighbors.

operations.rationale: Generic use bans, employee-access clauses and vague performance language were mistaken for exclusive-purpose rules, while repeated operative use restrictions and their governing introductions were omitted.
